description: Yoko Ono: Music of the Mind traces more than seven decades of Yoko Ono's groundbreaking career, from her early text-based works in the 1950s and '60s to recent large-scale installations informed by her ongoing campaigns for world peace. Organized in collaboration with Tate Modern, London, the exhibition—Ono's first solo museum exhibition in Southern California—explores her radical approach to art, language, and participation, challenging conventional ideas about the roles of artist and audience. Throughout the exhibition, Ono's celebrated "instruction" pieces invite you to become a part of the art itself. Tie a wish to an olive tree. Hammer a nail into a painting. A Road of Many Colors: Two Films on Oscar Rabin & Valentina Kropivnitskaya
description: Oscar Rabin wanted to paint. In the Soviet Union that made him a dissident. In 1974 Rabin helped organize an open-air show of unofficial art in Moscow. The authorities broke it up with bulldozers and water cannons. Images of the attack went around the world, and within weeks officials had to allow a second outdoor show. Thousands came. Several years later Rabin and his wife, the painter Valentina Kropivnitskaya, were forced into exile, and he was stripped of his Soviet citizenship. They started over in France. A Road of Many Colors tells their story in two documentaries written and directed by Alexander Smoljanski and Evgeny Tsymbal.
